summary.text: A 17-year-old boy with ileocolic Crohn’s disease diagnosed at age 6 years was initially treated with infliximab, which successfully managed the condition. He later developed treatment-related paradoxical psoriasis and recurrent skin abscesses refractory to antibiotic regimens, and intravenous ustekinumab induction was started in June 2022 with resolution of the abscesses and marked improvement in psoriasis.

In August 2022 he presented to the emergency department with dyspnea and chest pain, and chest radiographs confirmed a left-sided pneumothorax. A chest drain did not achieve full lung expansion, and chest CT showed a left-sided pneumothorax without associated bullae and a right apical bulla.

He underwent right bullectomy, resection of the left pulmonary apex and bilateral thoracoscopic abrasive pleurodesis, but complete expansion of the left lung was again not achieved. Ustekinumab was withdrawn, treatment was started exclusively with enteral nutrition and thiopurines, and the pneumothorax resolved completely. In April 2023 he had a new Crohn’s disease flare-up and intravenous ustekinumab was reinduced; 1 month later a recurrent left apical pneumothorax resolved with conservative management.

Because the pneumothorax followed ustekinumab initiation on two occasions and resolved after discontinuation, treatment was changed to vedolizumab, with good clinical progress and no further pulmonary complications after 1 year of follow-up. The patient has good adherence, good disease control and no new adverse effects; the authors consider ustekinumab can be related to the pulmonary complication.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract places the new Crohn’s disease flare-up "One year later" (after the sentence on resolution of the first pneumothorax), while the case text dates it to April 2023. Recorded as an ambiguity: the dated case-text fact is included and the abstract timing is review_only.
